title: Chrome and Edge Silently Increase Local AI Model Disk Requirements to 20GB, Browsers Are Becoming AI Inference Engines
excerpt: Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge have increased the disk space requirements for local AI models to 20GB. The browsers silently download these models in the back
content_html:
Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge have increased the disk space requirements for local AI models to 20GB. The browsers silently download these models in the background to support on-device AI features. In May of this year, Chrome was found to automatically download about 4GB of AI models to run AI features locally instead of uploading all data to Google's servers. Now, Google has quietly updated its official help documentation, raising the required free disk space from 4GB to about 20GB. This number is a prerequisite for downloading, but the actual model usage may be lower than this value.

Edge's requirements are largely consistent with Chrome, also requiring 20GB of available space, but with an additional GPU memory threshold: at least 5.5GB of video memory. Microsoft also stated that if available storage drops below 10GB, the models will be automatically deleted to ensure other browser functions run smoothly. Fortunately, both provide an option to turn off the feature—Chrome allows users to disable on-device AI features in the System settings, while Edge will automatically clean up models when storage is low. For users with ample storage, the impact is minimal, but it's worth noting that browsers secretly consume a significant amount of storage space, especially on devices with limited hard drive capacity.

Browsers Evolve into AI Runtime Environments

The sharp increase in demand for local AI models reflects a fundamental shift in the role of browsers. From a simple web rendering tool, to an extended ecosystem platform, and now to an on-device AI inference engine, browsers are taking on more computing tasks previously handled by operating systems or standalone applications. Running AI models locally offers core advantages such as reduced latency, protection of user privacy, and reduced reliance on cloud computing power, which explains why both Chrome and Edge are investing heavily in local AI.

However, the jump from 4GB to 20GB highlights that the size of local AI models is growing much faster than hardware storage improvements. For users with 256GB or smaller SSDs on lightweight laptops, 20GB of storage is no longer negligible, especially when multiple storage-heavy applications are installed simultaneously, increasing storage pressure. The additional requirement of 5.5GB of GPU memory for Edge further excludes many entry-level devices, meaning that the experience of local AI features will increasingly depend on hardware specifications. Browser developers need to find a more refined balance between AI feature richness and resource consumption, otherwise users may frequently choose to disable these features.

content_html_zh:
Google Chrome 和 Microsoft Edge 将本地 AI 模型的磁盘空间要求提高到 20GB。 浏览器会在后台静默下载这些模型，以支持设备上的人工智能功能。 今年5月，Chrome被发现自动下载约4GB的AI模型以在本地运行AI功能，而不是将所有数据上传到谷歌的服务器。 现在，谷歌已经悄然更新了官方帮助文档，将所需的可用磁盘空间从4GB提高到了20GB左右。 该数字是下载的前提条件，但实际模型使用情况可能会低于该值。

Edge 的要求与 Chrome 基本一致，同样需要 20GB 可用空间，但有一个额外的 GPU 内存阈值：至少 5.5GB 显存。 微软还表示，如果可用存储空间低于10GB，这些模型将被自动删除，以确保其他浏览器功能顺利运行。 幸运的是，两者都提供了关闭该功能的选项——Chrome 允许用户在系统设置中禁用设备上的 AI 功能，而 Edge 会在存储空间不足时自动清理模型。 对于拥有充足存储空间的用户来说，影响很小，但值得注意的是，浏览器会偷偷消耗大量存储空间，尤其是在硬盘容量有限的设备上。

浏览器演进为人工智能运行时环境

对本地人工智能模型的需求急剧增加反映了浏览器角色的根本转变。 从简单的网页渲染工具，到扩展的生态系统平台，再到现在的设备上人工智能推理引擎，浏览器正在承担更多以前由操作系统或独立应用程序处理的计算任务。 在本地运行 AI 模型具有减少延迟、保护用户隐私以及减少对云计算能力的依赖等核心优势，这解释了 Chrome 和 Edge 都大力投资本地 AI 的原因。

然而，从 4GB 到 20GB 的跃升凸显出本地 AI 模型大小的增长速度远远快于硬件存储的改进速度。 对于轻薄笔记本电脑上配备 256GB 或更小 SSD 的用户来说，20GB 存储空间已不再可以忽略不计，尤其是当同时安装多个存储密集型应用程序时，存储压力会增加。 Edge 对 5.5GB GPU 内存的额外要求进一步排除了许多入门级设备，这意味着本地 AI 功能的体验将越来越依赖于硬件规格。 浏览器开发者需要在AI功能丰富性和资源消耗之间找到更精细的平衡，否则用户可能会频繁选择禁用这些功能。
